record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Prove that the phase transition of two-dimensional φ⁴ theory lies in the same universality class, with the same critical exponents, as the two-dimensional Ising phase transition.

evidence.quote: the first significant result should be to prove that the phase transition of φ4 2 is in the same universality class (i.e. has the same critical exponents) than the Ising 2 phase transition.

artifact.category_tag: Constructive quantum field theory and critical phenomena
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional Euclidean φ⁴ scalar field theory on ℝ² (or, equivalently, on a sequence of finite lattice approximations whose lattice spacing tends to zero and volume tends to infinity), formally defined by the (Wick-renormalized) measure proportional to

  exp( − ∫_{ℝ²} ( ½ |∇φ(x)|² + ½ m² :φ(x)²: + g :φ(x)⁴: ) dx ) Dφ,

with mass parameter m² ∈ ℝ and coupling g > 0. As m² is varied (with g fixed, or along a suitable curve in the (m², g) parameter space), this model is known to undergo a phase transition between a unique-phase regime and a symmetry-broken regime exhibiting two pure phases related by the Z₂ symmetry φ ↦ −φ. Let the critical exponents (α, β, γ, δ, ν, η, …) describe the behavior near this transition of the specific heat, spontaneous magnetization ⟨φ⟩, susceptibility, magnetization at the critical point in an external field, correlation length, and two-point function decay at criticality, respectively.

Separately, consider the two-dimensional ferromagnetic nearest-neighbor Ising model on ℤ², whose critical exponents at the Onsager critical temperature T_c are known exactly: α = 0, β = 1/8, γ = 7/4, δ = 15, ν = 1, η = 1/4.

Problem: Prove rigorously that the phase transition of the two-dimensional φ⁴ Euclidean field theory lies in the same universality class as the two-dimensional Ising phase transition, and in particular that its critical exponents coincide with those of the two-dimensional Ising model listed above.
artifact.status_search_result: A rigorous proof that the 2D φ⁴ field theory critical point is in the Ising universality class with matching critical exponents is widely regarded as an outstanding open problem in constructive/mathematical quantum field theory. While numerical and renormalization-group evidence strongly supports this universality, no rigorous mathematical proof identifying the critical exponents of φ⁴₂ with those of the 2D Ising model is available in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Universality class - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Critical exponents are the same for all models in the class; the φ⁴ theory is conjecturally in the Ising class in d=2,3.
status_evidence.claim: Universality is established at the level of physics/RG, not as a rigorous theorem for φ⁴₂.

status_evidence.title: Critical Phenomena: field theoretical approach - Scholarpedia
status_evidence.snippet: Critical exponents expressed via scaling dimensions of operators in the CFT describing the phase transition.
status_evidence.claim: The identification of φ⁴ critical exponents with Ising values relies on RG/CFT arguments, not rigorous constructive proof.
